thread:
anya: FYI found a sandbox snapshot (s3://dev-sandbox/log-snapshots/2026-03-20.jsonl) used by DS team that includes Amplitude event payloads. Might include user emails.
sam: Wait that bucket is readonly to DS but isn't supposed to have raw PII. How did it get there?
josh: DS ingested a cleaned export but looks like the "user_properties.email" field was not stripped. I skimmed and saw ~1200 rows with plaintext emails.
ciso: If this maps to an active user request we need to treat as a DSAR. Pause any downstream sharing.
sec-ops-bot: Automated: Marking object with tag "sensitive=true". Recommend immediate object isolation: copy -> sse-kms, restrict ACL, create retention-exception ticket.
anya: I isolated a copy to priv-dsar-exports/6135790123/ and set SSE-KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/PROD-DSAR-01. Noted original object owner.
sam: Good. Can we produce an auditable package for Compliance? They want a chain-of-custody + evidence of access controls.
josh: Proposal: generate JSONL export -> compute sha256 manifest -> GPG sign -> upload signed.tar.gz to S3. Use short-lived creds for retrieval.
privacy-bot: Legal reminder: include requester proof, redaction decisions, and retention justification. If vendor retention exceeds org retention, open retention-exception.
ciso: Also need to confirm there was no exfil prior to isolation. Run an export-access scan for public presigned URLs and CloudFront logs.
sec-ops-bot: Suggested CLI steps:
```
# copy and encrypt
aws s3 cp s3://dev-sandbox/log-snapshots/2026-03-20.jsonl s3://priv-dsar-exports/6135790123/2026-03-20.jsonl --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/PROD-DSAR-01
# manifest
sha256sum 2026-03-20.jsonl > manifest.sha256
# tar + gpg
tar czf 6135790123-signed.tar.gz 2026-03-20.jsonl manifest.sha256
gpg --output 6135790123-signed.tar.gz.sig --sign 6135790123-signed.tar.gz
```
keepsam: Note: presigned URL only via JIT role retrieval, expiry 1h.
anya: KMS key policy snippet for reference (draft):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowDSARExportService",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456:role/dsar-exporter"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*","kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:dsar_id": "6135790123"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
sam: A couple of checks: 1) Confirm CloudTrail recorded GetObject events for the original object. 2) Create an evidence log entry in PrivEvidence store.
josh: I'll run a PII detector (PII-FILTER v2) over the isolated copy and paste results here.
ciso: Open retention-exception now and loop in Legal. If vendor retention applies we need a documented justification to keep beyond 90 days.
anya: Created ticket RE-1102: https://re.redwood/retention-exceptions/RE-1102 (cc legal, compliance).
sec-ops-bot: Export packaging requires two approvers: security and legal. Also: TTL on S3 artifact set to 48h auto-delete unless RE-1102 approved.
privacy-bot: Reminder: redact any third-party tokens and remove vendor debug headers before signing. Also include the redaction log.
sam: Action items: Josh -> PII scan & manifest, Anya -> upload GPG-signed package + evidence entry, CISO -> confirm there was no prior external access.
